Consumers were rewired coherently: resolveEfficiencyPolicyDecision returns {policy, override} and the status reaches pr prepare (src/pr-manager.js:11946+), the authorize artifact, the text summary, and throwReviewDispatchStop (src/agent-review.js:3890+). Noted residual: a write failure after the document is written leaves an orphan tracked doc, but enforcement still refuses the override, so the diff over-claims rather than under-enforces.

Independent adjudicator re-judged both previously-unsound defects as genuinely fixed on their merits. (1) isPathGitIgnored (src/decision-records.js:479-499) distinguishes exit 0 / exit 1 / 'not a git repository' / everything-else-throws, and critically the BGT-S-3 fixture now runs git init (test/decision-records.test.js:335) so the guard actually executes instead of being dead under test. (2) findExistingBudgetApprovalDoc (src/decision-records.js:283-292) keys reuse on the (story_id, digest8) suffix, and the new date-reuse test renames the document to a 2020 prefix and asserts exactly one file survives a re-record. Minor residual: the hand-written backfill document lacks decision_id and uses a date-only approved_at, so the tracked channel holds two frontmatter shapes with no validator -- cosmetic today, brittle if anything ever parses it.

Independent adjudicator: an unauthorized override is inert rather than fatal and falls back to the tighter base policy (src/delivery-efficiency-guardrail.js:87-90), so no state can go over-green; the inert status surfaces as budget_override_unauthorized debt in summarizeEfficiencyDebt and inline in the dispatch-stop message, closing the 'stop says budget_exceeded while config says otherwise' misdiagnosis. Failure to read decision records degrades to no-decisions, hence inert, hence base budget: fail-closed. The growing GRANDFATHERED_OVERRIDE_DIGESTS map re-authorizes by content digest only and requires a visible code diff, which is the designed constraint.

The Story doc states 7 concrete acceptance criteria BGT-S-1..S-7 with an evidenced problem statement; each criterion maps to a named passing test in the acceptance spec, which the adjudicator ran (7/7 pass at 1f6c38a9).

Independently confirmed the stated reality: git check-ignore shows .vibepro/pr/** ignored and docs/management/decisions/** tracked, and the flow_replay spec executes end-to-end through the real CLI (BGT-E2E-1/E2E-2 in test/decision-records.test.js, 16/16 pass). Nit: in this worktree the ignore rule matched .git/info/exclude:23 rather than .gitignore:5 as the Story text says.

The invariants in the spec (fail-before-write; digest identity; no-grant path unchanged) each have executable counterparts. resolveBudgetOverrideAuthority in src/budget-override-authority.js:187 reads approval with optional chaining, so the added budget_approval: null field cannot change existing resolution.

The Story boundary explicitly excludes in-band forgery and fs-existence checks in the resolver, and the resolver was confirmed to have no fs dependency: src/budget-override-authority.js imports only node:crypto.

Both negative paths are genuinely exercised, not merely asserted: BGT-S-3 gitignored path, and the undeterminable-gitignore-status case that fails the grant instead of falling back. Both passed and correspond to the real branches at src/decision-records.js:307 and :484-500.

The adjudicator re-ran the cited replay command rather than trusting the recorded token; 7/7 acceptance cases pass at this head, and BGT-S-6/S-7 assert against real repo files rather than fixtures. The backfill digest was independently recomputed and matches the document override_digest.

The only output-shape change is budget_approval: null, which BGT-S-4 concedes explicitly rather than claiming bit-identity. No CLI flags were added, and the en/ja CLI reference lines are generated from a single source (scripts/generate-cli-reference.mjs:74-75) so they cannot drift.

Doc-write precedes store-write, so the only crash-window residue is an orphan tracked document with no effective grant, which is the fail-safe direction. Re-recording is idempotent via findExistingBudgetApprovalDoc suffix lookup (src/decision-records.js:283-306), and there are no locks or workers that could deadlock.

git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD is 27 files / 3148 insertions across 48 commits spanning three story docs; whether that stack is one reviewable judgment is a human reviewer-capacity call. Additionally the Story verification section claims the parent Story doc is not edited in this PR, yet commit e327cc75 edits docs/management/stories/active/story-vibepro-owner-gated-budget-override.md, so the Story text is inaccurate on this point and a human should decide whether to correct it or split.

grep -rn management/decisions over src/ and scripts/ shows no production code parses these documents, so a not_required classification is justified. Noted latent gap: the frontmatter is built by unescaped interpolation of free-text grantor, so a grantor containing a newline or colon would emit malformed YAML for any future or external parser.

This change moves evidence toward the tracked surface and cannot produce a misleading green: the failure path refuses to write the workspace record at all, verified by the BGT-S-3 and undeterminable-status tests, rather than recording a grant whose mirror is missing.

The three-state flow declared in the spec (no_grant / granted / refused) is each covered by a passing acceptance case, including the idempotent granted-to-granted re-record that reuses the existing path instead of minting a stale duplicate document.
